text:
morgan: Quick question — for canary rollouts, are we okay with a hands-free fallback that triggers solely on service errors (5xx / high latency) or do we force an operator confirmation? :thinking:

jess: leaning toward automated for critical failures, but only if the UI shows a clear audit trail and an undo. we don't want silent flips.

samir: propose a middle ground: auto-trigger + a short cooldown + operator notif + single-click revert. example config i've been noodling: 

```yaml
fallback_policy:
  triggers:
    - name: high_5xx_ratio
      expr: http_5xx_ratio > 0.05
      window: 60s
      occurrences: 3
    - name: sustained_tail_latency
      expr: p95_latency_ms > 1200
      window: 3m
  mode: soft_degrade    # options: hard_switch | soft_degrade | sample_redirect
  cool_down: 120s
  audit_retention_days: 90
```

morgan: that looks reasonable. what's "soft_degrade" in practice?

jess: soft_degrade = divert X% of traffic to fallback model/region and keep the rest on canary for data. less risky than full cut. shows partial impact in console.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary 2024-02-16T12:14:05Z: health checks failing (5xx spikes). Suggested action: soft_degrade -> 25% redirect.

taylor: on the UX side, we need two visible things: 1) a timeline showing recent triggers + metrics used, 2) a single "why" affordance (drill into exact rule + last matching samples). also show estimated cost/latency delta when degrading.

leo: worry: oscillation if metric bounces. add hysteresis and require minimum time at degraded state before re-eval. also tag every fallback with a "reason" and unique event id so audits and playbacks are trivial.

samir: +1 to event ids. telemetry should export fallback events to tracing (trace_id) and to alerting so SREs can subscribe. also keep a sample of user requests routed during degrade for QA.

jess: ui mock idea: when auto-trigger occurs, show a compact toast: "Auto-degraded to soft (25%) due to p95 > 1200ms — Undo | Details". clicking Details opens a side panel with: trigger eval, last 10 samples, buttons: revert now, increase degrade, mark as known issue.

morgan: ops questions — defaults: should we enable auto fallback for new tenants? my vote: enabled with conservative defaults, and require a check-box in the onboarding to opt-out.

taylor: agree on conservative opt-in/out. also expose telemetry sampling rate and ability to forward events to tenant logging.

leo: implementation note: add a minimal schema for the fallback event to keep logs searchable: {event_id, ts, rollout_id, trigger_name, mode, percent, metrics_snapshot, operator}. small but important.

morgan: ok can we summarize next steps?

jess: 1) ship a UI toast + details panel mock (taylor)
2) implement cool_down + hysteresis in policy engine (samir/eng-runtime)
3) audit event schema + tracing hook (leo)
4) default conservative policy for new tenants + opt-out (product)

samir: i'll draft a prototype policy schema and a lightweight simulator to show oscillation risk.

taylor: i'll throw together a 2-panel mock and a small flow for the toast->details->undo.

morgan: perfect. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [audit-bot] Note: when the policy is auto-enabled, fallback events will be retained for 90 days by default (configurable).

jess: can someone add a short runbook snippet explaining "when auto-degrade happens" for oncall? 1-2 bullets.

leo: i'll drop a 3-line runbook in this thread tomorrow.

morgan: awesome — we'll reconvene after the mocks and protos.
